newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds sag, spreads widen modestly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds sag, spreads widen modestly.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities continued their slide in late-afternoon trade on Wednesday.

Pass-through yield spreads to Treasuries were stuck on the wide side following the Treasury's afternoon auction of $12 billion of 10-year securities, the second and last part of its quarterly refunding effort.
The 10-year averaged a yield of 6.740 percent and a high yield of 6.759 percent.
In its Beige Book summary of national economic activity, the Federal Reserve bank said the economy "generally continued to expand at a moderate rate through March and April."
Specifically, the labor markets remained tight and employers throughout the country reported shortages of qualified help, the central bank said.
"Tight labor markets and shortages of qualified help persisted throughout much of the nation in March and April," it said.
Mortgage trading activity picked up slightly as the Mortgage Bankers Association concluded its National Secondary Market conference in San Francisco, traders said.
"A lot of the (players) that haven't been selling for the last couple of days have come back (and) started selling so volume is up a little bit," one trader said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was off 11/32 at 99-04/32, yielding 102 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 14/32 at 99-05/32 and Freddie Mac paper was off 9/32 at 99-13/32.
Five-year Treasuries were off 10/32 at 6.63 percent, and 10-year notes were down 20/32 at 6.76 percent.
